grades.rationale: Life Link explicitly distributes harm between caster and target for one minute, reducing the first damage instance each round and causing equal unavoidable caster HP loss. It can be dismissed and ends on caster unconsciousness.
grades.adjudicationReason: This is direct magical injury distribution and can be used between consenting allies. Ordinary caps, duration and absence of an obligatory willingness tag do not make the requested function indirect.

grades.rationale: Embrace the Pain is a barbarian reaction that grapples or disarms the attacker after being damaged. It supplies no ally bond, magical distribution or transferred injury.
grades.adjudicationReason: A pain-themed title and generic taking-damage trigger are insufficient for a substantive injury-sharing relationship.

grades.rationale: Empathic Link creates a genuine magical bond sharing emotions with a willing creature over up to a mile; it transfers no physical injury or damage.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual interpersonal magical sharing is substantively related but cannot fulfill the authored injury-distribution function. Emotional communion is not promoted to HP transfer.

grades.rationale: We Are One coordinates a companion’s shared space, cover and attacks, without transferring harm or establishing magic that distributes injury.
grades.adjudicationReason: Generic shared positioning/teamwork is not a source-backed injury-sharing component. The title and shared wording alone do not merit related relevance.

grades.rationale: Share Life forms a magical ten-minute link: target takes half of HP damage and caster takes the remainder without mitigation. Distance over30feet or either reaching0HP ends it.
grades.adjudicationReason: This directly fulfills magical injury distribution between consenting allies. Explicit duration/distance/end conditions remain, while lack of a compulsory willingness tag does not prohibit consensual use or make the route indirect.

grades.rationale: Bonding Meal is actual food-preparation magic whose effect shares memories and social insight with friends. It does not preserve food or prolong edibility.
grades.adjudicationReason: Real magical cooking is substantively related food magic, but the social effect is not useful for preserving food. The actual source—not a mere meal word—supports relatedness.

grades.rationale: Restore Ground makes plants healthier and more fruitful for a year while removing artificial objects and structures. It does not prevent harvested food from spoiling.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual plant-health/production magic provides a substantive adjacent food-production relationship; it does not establish stored-food preservation or useful food-safety treatment.

grades.rationale: Overstuff magically supplies a meal’s nourishment directly to a creature and may sicken it. It creates no preserved food for future consumption.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual magical nourishment is substantive adjacent food magic, below useful for the preservation intent. Harm to the eater is not automatically reversal of food preservation.

grades.rationale: Daemonic Infector has actually prepared Purify Food and Drink, removing contaminants and making food safe to eat. The spell explicitly cannot prevent future decay/spoilage.
grades.adjudicationReason: Both opinions missed either the prepared capability or the authored allowance for useful qualified adjacent food-safety uses. Actual preparation/association proves this concrete route; do not claim preservation or infer it from unrelated poison abilities.

grades.rationale: Ghoulish Cravings is actual magic affecting raw-meat consumption and hunger, but does not change food safety or storage life.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual magical food-consumption mechanics are substantively related, but no preservation/edibility route is supplied. It does not spoil food or actively negate preservation, so the opposite flag is false.

grades.rationale: Food Preservation really extends alchemical food’s storage life using pickling, alcohol or fermentation, with explicit item/proficiency limits. It is an alchemical technique rather than magic.
grades.adjudicationReason: The actual preservation function is substantive, while the authored intent explicitly seeks magic. Do not infer magic from an infused/alchemical item; this is related below useful for that requirement.

grades.rationale: Jonis has actually prepared Purify Food and Drink, making contaminated food safe to consume but leaving future natural decay/spoilage unchanged.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual preparation corrects the primary’s missing food capability. The authored criteria allow qualified adjacent uses; restored food safety is useful with explicit lack of preservation, consistently with other sources owning this same spell.

grades.rationale: Prestidigitation can cool, warm or flavor a pound of nonliving material while sustained. It contains no lasting food-storage or anti-spoilage rule.
grades.adjudicationReason: Real food-processing/cooling magic is substantive related content, but inventing refrigeration strength or sustained anti-spoilage would exceed the source. It is not a useful preservation route as written.

grades.rationale: Timeless Salts prevent an object’s decay and ordinary pest consumption for one week, subject to size/Bulk and dispersal limits. The consumable is explicitly alchemical, without a magical trait.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual preservation can apply to food and is substantive. The required magic is absent; mentioning magical revival as a downstream use does not make these salts magical.

grades.rationale: This background teaches Survival, Cooking Lore and Forager, with actual culinary experience handling difficult/hardy ingredients. It grants no magical food preservation.
grades.adjudicationReason: The source is substantively about preparing/sourcing edible food, rather than an incidental inventory noun. It fails the preservation and magic requirements, so remains related below useful.

grades.rationale: Glue Bullet genuinely sticks a target to a nearby surface and may immobilize it, but is fired ammunition without ceiling placement or an autonomous ceiling hazard.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual adhesive restraint is a substantive component. A possible improvised ceiling setup is not authored, so this fails the combined intent rather than becoming qualified useful.

grades.rationale: Living Tar’s actual adhesive mass holds struck weapons and stuck creatures, but its cave-ooze source describes no ceiling placement or overhead adhesive trap.
grades.adjudicationReason: The sticky-restraint component is real, while ceiling context is absent. Creature family alone is not the rejection; the unfulfilled spatial component is.

grades.rationale: This actual trap deploys blades from ceiling, floor and walls, causing slashing/bleeding rather than adhesive restraint.
grades.adjudicationReason: A ceiling-origin hazard is a substantive partial component, consistently with the7–8 variant. Missing adhesion keeps it below useful.

grades.rationale: Sticky Poison uses actual increased viscosity to retain a poisonous coating on a weapon. It does not glue creatures in place and has no ceiling context.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual sticky-substance coating mechanics are related, rather than title-only coincidence. The recipient/function differ from adhesive creature restraint, so it is not useful.

grades.rationale: The pressure-triggered darts are actually mounted on the ceiling and attack creatures, with poison rather than adhesive restraint.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual ceiling hazard context supplies a substantive component. It fails the sticky-restraint requirement rather than being unrelated.

grades.rationale: The major furniture archway is piled to the high ceiling, collapses and can bury/suffocate creatures. It has no adhesive substance.
grades.adjudicationReason: An overhead collapsing obstruction with actual trapping is related, consistently with the ordinary variant. It does not establish a sticky ceiling or useful adhesive route.

grades.rationale: Mimic’s adhesive slime grabs creatures that touch or strike it, and its disguised Object Lesson can trap an interacting creature automatically. No ceiling context is authored.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual adhesive ambush mechanics supply a component, but a ceiling installation would be invented. Cross-family relevance is allowed; missing ceiling context is the reason it is not useful.

grades.rationale: This ceiling-mounted chemical trap sprays solvents/detergents that deal acid damage and can blind. It has no adhesive restraint.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual overhead hazardous substance delivery is a substantive ceiling component, without the requested adhesive function. Solvent chemistry is not assumed to reverse a particular adhesive effect absent source evidence.

grades.rationale: The actual pressure-triggered crossbow drops from a ceiling panel and fires bolts; its attacks use no adhesive substance.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual ceiling trap context is substantive, but no sticky-restraint capability appears. It remains below useful.

grades.rationale: Five actual ceiling nozzles release acidic poison gas that fills the room and damages creatures/objects. It does not adhere or restrain.
grades.adjudicationReason: An authored ceiling hazard is a substantive partial component. Poison gas is not an adhesive workaround and is not useful for the combined intent.

grades.rationale: Constricting Hall uses four elastic walls to strike creatures and knock them prone. It establishes neither a ceiling mechanism nor adhesion.
grades.adjudicationReason: Generic hallway hazard and altered wall texture are insufficient for either requested component. Elastic pummeling is not source-backed sticky restraint.

grades.rationale: The suite’s actual glowing ceiling runes seal doors and activate hostile magical effects. No rune applies adhesive restraint.
grades.adjudicationReason: Actual ceiling hazard context and chamber trapping make it substantively related; door deadbolts are not sticky substance, so this is below useful.

grades.rationale: Actual ceiling sprinklers react to fire and shower frozen retardant, dealing cold damage and ending persistent fire. Nothing adheres to or restrains creatures.
grades.adjudicationReason: This supplies a substantive ceiling hazard component only. Extinguishing fire is not an opposite of the requested sticky-ceiling function, so the separate flag remains false.

grades.rationale: Green Slime actually clings overhead, drops onto passing prey and coats it so normal removal no longer works, causing escalating drain. It directly adheres to creatures from a ceiling.
grades.adjudicationReason: The authored criteria require adherence OR trapping through sticky substance, without demanding an immobilized condition. Actual durable coating fulfills that direct function; dangerous damage rather than simple immobilization is not an indirectness penalty.

grades.adjudicationReason: This is the requested returning thrown weapon itself, with its actual miss condition preserved. Mechanical trait context supplies behavior omitted from the main description.

grades.rationale: Chakri has the actual recovery and thrown traits. The pinned recovery definition returns it after an unsuccessful thrown Strike; wrist loading is an additional separate benefit.
grades.adjudicationReason: Both reviewers missed the trait’s actual return mechanic. The source-backed weapon directly fulfills returning-after-throw behavior, with the miss-only condition retained rather than assuming return on every hit.
